rule: Depth needs both the size and the spacing of repeated objects to shrink as they recede.
The closer a surface is to the eye level or to the vanishing direction, the flatter it appears.
A circle in perspective is an ellipse whose widest point is offset from the centre of its perspective square, toward the near side.
Ellipses do not have points: the ends of a foreshortened circle stay rounded.
Establish the size and big proportions of the whole drawing in light lines first, before details.
